title: Projective Bott--Samelson galleries and torus-fixed subexpressions
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and with every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group having finite central kernel an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive scheme-theoretic commutator subgroups become trivial, and central means commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B\subseteq G$, with $B$ a Borel subgroup, and use $Q=G/B$, the roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ and simple roots $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r$ of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $W=N_G(T)(F)/T(F)$ and choose representatives $n_w$ as in [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts]. Write $s_i=s_{\alpha_i}$ for the reflections of [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], and $\ell(w)$ for the minimum number of simple reflections with product $w$. Let $\mathbf i=(i_1,\ldots,i_m)$ be any finite word, not necessarily reduced. Let $P_i$ be the closed subgroup generated by $B$ and the root subgroup $U_{-\alpha_i}$ of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. It has $P_i(K)=B(K)\sqcup B(K)n_{s_i}B(K)$ for every algebraically closed extension $K/F$. The fppf quotient of $P_{i_1}\times_F\cdots\times_F P_{i_m}$ by the right $B^m$-action $$(p_1,\ldots,p_m)(b_1,\ldots,b_m)=(p_1b_1,b_1^{-1}p_2b_2,\ldots,b_{m-1}^{-1}p_mb_m)$$ is represented by a smooth integral projective $F$-scheme $Z_{\mathbf i}$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-pc-projective-morphism]. Here fppf means faithfully flat coverings locally of finite presentation. For $m=0$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}F$. It is obtained by successive Zariski locally trivial $\mathbf P^1_F$-fibrations [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Multiplication gives a $B$-equivariant proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] endpoint morphism $$\mu_{\mathbf i}:Z_{\mathbf i}\longrightarrow Q,\qquad[p_1,\ldots,p_m]\longmapsto p_1\cdots p_m B,$$ where $B$ acts on the first factor. The locus with every $p_j\in Bn_{s_{i_j}}B$ is open dense and isomorphic to $\mathbf A_F^m$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. If the word is reduced with product $w$, the image of this open locus under $\mu_{\mathbf i}$ is $C_w=Bn_wB/B$. The fixed $K$-points for the induced $T$-action are exactly the $2^m$ classes $$[n_{s_{i_1}}^{\epsilon_1},\ldots,n_{s_{i_m}}^{\epsilon_m}],\qquad \epsilon_j\in\{0,1\},$$ and their endpoints are $e_{s_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1}\cdots s_{i_m}^{\epsilon_m}}$, where $e_x=n_xB\in Q$ for $x\in W$. Fixed means fixed after every commutative algebra extension, and the fixed-point assertion concerns points, not a reducedness claim for the fixed subscheme. All assertions hold in every characteristic.

proof.text:
For $I=\{\alpha_i\}$, [lem-sfb-standard-parabolic-levi-charts] supplies the generated subgroup $P_i$ and represented quotient $H_i=G/P_i$. Apply [lem-sfb-minimal-parabolic-flag-projection] to each $\alpha_i$; the hypotheses agree with those of this item. This supplies the specified subgroup $P_i$, its two double cosets, and the smooth projective locally trivial map $q_i:Q\to H_i=G/P_i$. Construct by induction $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}F$, with endpoint $x_0=B$, and
$$Z_j=Z_{j-1}\times_{H_{i_j}}Q,$$
where the first map to $H_{i_j}$ is $q_{i_j}\circ x_{j-1}$; let $x_j$ be the second projection. Fibre products exist by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $Z_j$ represents tuples of flags $(x_1,\ldots,x_j)$ with $q_{i_a}(x_{a-1})=q_{i_a}(x_a)$ for each $a$. The map forgetting $x_j$ is the base change of $q_{i_j}$ and so is a Zariski locally trivial projective-line fibration.

proof.text: Identify this scheme with the quotient in the statement. Send $(p_1,\ldots,p_m)$ to the cumulative flags $x_j=p_1\cdots p_jB$. The stated action changes the cumulative product $g_j$ to $g_jb_j$, so leaves each flag unchanged. Conversely, locally on any test scheme lift all $x_j$ to $g_j\in G$, using the Zariski local sections of $G\to Q$ in [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts]; put $g_0=1$ and $p_j=g_{j-1}^{-1}g_j$. The equality $g_{j-1}P_{i_j}=g_jP_{i_j}$ implies $p_j\in P_{i_j}$ as a scheme-valued assertion, by the right $P_{i_j}$-torsor identity in [lem-sfb-standard-parabolic-levi-charts]. Replacing lifts $g_j$ by $g_jb_j$ changes $p_j$ to $b_{j-1}^{-1}p_jb_j$, with $b_0=1$, exactly the prescribed action. These formulas are inverse on local representatives and agree on overlaps, hence give inverse morphisms of fppf sheaves. The cumulative-flag construction therefore represents the required quotient, including the empty product. Simultaneous left multiplication of all flags by $b\in B$ preserves the first condition because $bB=B$, and preserves every remaining condition by equivariance of $q_i$. In quotient coordinates this is the action on the first factor, and the endpoint is $x_m$.

proof.text: Prove smoothness and projectivity by induction on $j$. Both hold for $Z_0$. Smooth base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) and composition [lem-trf-smooth-composition] show $Z_j\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is smooth. Projective base change [lem-pc-projective-base-change] and H-projective composition [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] give a projective-space embedding of $Z_j$ over $F$. It is quasi-compact since it is closed in a finite-dimensional projective space over a field, so it satisfies the blueprint's projectivity convention. Each fibre of $Z_j\to Z_{j-1}$ is a nonempty projective line. For integrality, an affine trivializing open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ in the integral base has preimage $\mathbf P^1_A$, covered by the two spectra of the domains $A[t]$; their intersection $\operatorname{Spec}A[t,t^{-1}]$ is nonempty. Thus each such preimage is reduced and irreducible. Preimages of any two nonempty trivializing opens meet since the base is irreducible and the fibres are nonempty. These preimages cover, so $Z_j$ is reduced, irreducible and nonempty. This proves integrality inductively. Finally $Z_m$ is proper over $F$ by [lem-pc-projective-proper], and $Q$ is separated over $F$ by its properness in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Apply [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] to conclude that the endpoint is proper.

proof.text:
The rank-one coordinate statement [lem-sfb-minimal-parabolic-flag-projection] gives the open set $Bn_{s_i}B$ in $P_i$ and its unique coordinates $p=u_{\alpha_i}(a)n_{s_i}b$. The condition that every factor belongs to its open double coset is invariant under the quotient action. Normalize $p_1$ to $u_{\alpha_{i_1}}(a_1)n_{s_{i_1}}$ by choosing $b_1$; absorb the residual $B$-factor into $p_2$ and repeat. At each stage the rank-one coordinates are unique and regular, including their inverse, so this gives inverse morphisms
$$\mathbf A_F^m\longleftrightarrow Z_m^\circ,\qquad (a_1,\ldots,a_m)\longmapsto[u_{\alpha_{i_1}}(a_1)n_{s_{i_1}},\ldots,u_{\alpha_{i_m}}(a_m)n_{s_{i_m}}].$$
Openness can be checked on the local quotient lifts in step 2: it is there the intersection of inverse images of the indicated open double cosets. The open is nonempty (all $a_j=0$ works), and $Z_m$ is integral by step 3, so it is dense. No reducedness of the word was used.

proof.text:
If the word is reduced, [lem-sfb-simple-bruhat-double-coset-product] gives, over every algebraically closed extension $K/F$,
$$B(K)n_{s_{i_1}}B(K)\cdots B(K)n_{s_{i_m}}B(K)=B(K)n_wB(K).$$
The endpoint formula therefore gives exactly $C_w(K)=B(K)n_wB(K)/B(K)$ as the image of $Z_m^\circ(K)$. Thus the image assertion concerns this open locus. For $m=0$ it says that the unique endpoint is $B=C_1$. In terms of the reduced locally closed cell structures of [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts], these are the same underlying image; no claim that the image of the entire proper $Z_m$ is the nonclosed cell is being made.

proof.text: For an algebraically closed extension $K/F$, induct on the gallery length to compute the $T$-fixed $K$-points. At length zero there is one, with endpoint $B$. A fixed gallery projects equivariantly to a fixed prefix. By induction write that prefix in the indicated subexpression form, and let $h=n_{s_{i_1}}^{\epsilon_1}\cdots n_{s_{i_{m-1}}}^{\epsilon_{m-1}}\in N_G(T)(F)$ be its cumulative representative. The remaining fibre is $hP_{i_m}/B$. Left multiplication by $h^{-1}$ identifies its $T$-action with that on $P_{i_m}/B$, with $t$ replaced by $h^{-1}th$. By [lem-sfb-minimal-parabolic-flag-projection], this line has the point $B$ and the affine chart $a\mapsto u_{\alpha_{i_m}}(a)n_{s_{i_m}}B$. The chart action is multiplication by the character $\alpha_{i_m}(h^{-1}th)$, which is nontrivial since normalizer conjugation is an automorphism of $T$. For a fixed $K$-point its coordinate must satisfy $(\alpha_{i_m}(h^{-1}th)-1)a=0$ over every $K$-algebra. In the Laurent polynomial coordinate ring of the split torus the nonzero Laurent polynomial $\alpha_{i_m}(h^{-1}th)-1$ cannot be annihilated by a nonzero scalar $a\in K$. Hence $a=0$. The two and only two fixed points of this fibre are therefore $hB$ and $hn_{s_{i_m}}B$. Appending $1$ or $n_{s_{i_m}}$ gives the two desired classes. Their endpoint $n_{s_{i_1}}^{\epsilon_1}\cdots n_{s_{i_m}}^{\epsilon_m}B$ is $e_x$ for $x=s_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1}\cdots s_{i_m}^{\epsilon_m}$, since this product and $n_x$ represent the same element of $W$ and so differ by an element of $T(F)\subseteq B(F)$. Distinct prefixes remain distinct on projection, and the two extensions of one prefix are distinct in its projective-line fibre; thus the count doubles from $2^{m-1}$ to $2^m$. Conversely these choices are fixed because both rank-one flags are fixed as group-scheme points. This character calculation works also when the differential of a root vanishes, and proves only the asserted statement about points.
